# VeerOS — Raspberry Pi 5 boot configuration
# Place this file on the FAT32 boot partition of the SD card.
#
# The RPi firmware reads this before loading the kernel.
# See: https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/config_txt.html

# ── Core settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Boot in 64-bit (AArch64) mode — required for VeerOS
arm_64bit=1

# Load our kernel image (default is kernel8.img for 64-bit)
kernel=kernel8.img

# Disable Linux device-tree overlay — we're bare-metal
device_tree=

# ── UART console ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Enable mini-UART on GPIO 14/15 (pins 8/10) at 115200 baud.
# This gives you the VeerOS shell over a serial adapter.
enable_uart=1

# Fix mini-UART clock so baud rate is stable
core_freq=250
core_freq_min=250

# ── GPU / display ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Allocate 64 MB to the VideoCore (enough for a framebuffer console)
gpu_mem=64

# Disable firmware splash screen for faster boot
disable_splash=1

# ── Hardware ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Enable I2C on GPIO 2/3 (bus 1, header pins 3/5)
dtparam=i2c_arm=on

# Enable SPI on GPIO 7-11 (bus 0, header pins 19/21/23/24/26)
dtparam=spi=on

# Disable Bluetooth (frees up the PL011 UART if needed later)
dtoverlay=disable-bt

# ── Boot behaviour ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Don't wait for a keyboard — go straight to kernel
boot_delay=0

# Disable overscan compensation (clean framebuffer edges)
disable_overscan=1
